claims.statement: The source keeps a stroke pulse of 0.189 s (317 strokes per minute); counted in groups of 2 pulses this is 158 beats per minute (a counting convention; the matra is not established from audio).
The 53 strokes of the segment occupy 53 of 55 slots of that pulse grid; the median distance of a stroke from the fitted grid is 10 ms.
The bass pattern repeats every 12 pulses (about 2.27 s; autocorrelation 0.65). The taal is not identified by the system.
The bass drum (bayan) is sounded on 21 of 53 strokes and withheld on the rest; one cycle reads BBB--.B---B- (B = bass stroke, - = stroke without bass, . = empty pulse).
The pulse is steady: intervals between strokes, divided by their pulse count, vary by 11.3% (coefficient of variation).
An audio model labelled the strokes as: Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge Ge ... (model inference, not confirmed by an expert).

The source uses 3 distinct stroke timbres (silhouette 0.25); each stroke is assigned to a timbre class by k-means on its MFCC and spectral features (Class A (mostly 'Ge', inferred); Class B (mostly 'Ge', inferred); Class C (mostly 'Ge', inferred)).
Stroke classes correspond mostly to bols: Class A (mostly 'Ge', inferred); Class B (mostly 'Ge', inferred); Class C (mostly 'Ge', inferred) (inferred by audio model; not confirmed by an expert).

summary: A 12 s tabla segment (53 strokes, pulse 0.189 s, bass on 21 strokes, bass pattern repeating every 12 pulses, 3 timbre classes). Timing and bass are measured deterministically from the audio; bols and taal are not asserted.
title: Tabla stroke pattern: tempo, grid and bayan
